newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures end lower, Oct breaks support late.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures end lower, Oct breaks support late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures settled several cents lower Tuesday, suppressed early by news that Hurricane Hortense would likely veer away from the Gulf Coast, industry sources said.

October finished 10.7 cents weaker at $1.791 per million British thermal units after breaking through the $1.80 support level shortly before its close. November settled down 8.3 cents at $2.04, englarging the Oct/Nov spread to 24.9 cents.
Traders said the restoration of some power in North Carolina after Hurricane Fran also contributed to the softness.

With the $1.80 level erased, support in October was now pegged at $1.78, just a half-cent shy of this session's low. Next support was seen at $1.735 and $1.68. Traders said resistance was first at $1.84, which was the previous support level. Next resistance was seen in the low-$1.90s, then $1.955.

In the cash market, prices were mostly stable today in the high-$1.70s to low-$1.80s on the U.S. Gulf Coast pipes as many buyers took the time to replenish depleted storage inventories and heard news that there was a leak on Columbia Gas's northern Virginia line. Midcontinent prices gained more than five cents to reach the low-$1.70s as some last-minute buyers scrambled for additional supplies.
NYMEX's October Permian contract settled six cents lower at $1.515, also extending its losses in late trading. NYMEX said 62 lots exchanged hands.
Permian cash prices were talked in the high-$1.50s to low-$1.60s.
On the KCBT, October finished 6.8 cents lower at $1.592, while other months were down about two to seven cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 19.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
In contrast, physical prices at Waha held fairly strong in the high-$1.60s to low-$1.70s, boosted by some pipeline maintenance.
At 1400 EDT, Hortense was just offshore El Macao on the northeast coast of the Dominican Republic. Still on the same path, the storm was moving west-northwest at 12 miles per hour.
